records.content_text:
A **pyramid** is an object that has a polygon as its base and sides that **converge** (meet each other) at one single point. The sides are *not* perpendicular to the base.

There are many real life objects in the form of a pyramid. The pyramids of Egypt are well known.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-024.png]

A pile of eggs can be stacked in a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-025.png]

The roof of a house can be in the shape of a pyramid.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-026.png]

A pyramid can have any polygon, for example a rectangle, a pentagon, or a hexagon, as its base.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-027.png]

We will focus on a pyramid that has a square as its base.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-028.png]

The properties of a pyramid are:

- A square-based pyramid has five *faces*.

- A square-based pyramid has a square as a *base*.

- The side faces are four equal isosceles triangles.

- The faces of a pyramid meet each other at an *edge*.

- A square-based pyramid has eight edges: four around the base and four formed by the triangular side faces.

- The edges of a pyramid meet each other at a *vertex*.

- A square-based pyramid has five vertices: four at the base and one at the top where the triangles meet each other.

The top vertex has a special name. The edges of the triangles that form the side faces converge at a vertex called the **apex**.

We call a pyramid a "right pyramid" if the line between the apex and the centre of the base is perpendicular to the base.

placement.rationale: This record defines pyramid, converge, and apex.

records.evidence_quote: **pyramid** A pyramid is a 3D object that has a polygon as its base. The side faces are triangles that meet each other at one single point, the apex. **converge** To converge is to move towards each other and to meet at one point. **apex** The apex is the top-most point that is furthest from the base of a 3D object.
records.content_text:
**pyramid** A pyramid is a 3D object that has a polygon as its base. The side faces are triangles that meet each other at one single point, the apex.

**converge** To converge is to move towards each other and to meet at one point.

**apex** The apex is the top-most point that is furthest from the base of a 3D object.

One of the faces is flat and the other face is curved. - The *base* of a cone is a flat circle. - [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-039.png] - A cone has only one side face, and this face
records.content_text:
The properties of a cone are:

- A cone has two *faces*. One of the faces is flat and the other face is curved.
- The *base* of a cone is a flat circle.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-039.png]
- A cone has only one side face, and this face is curved.
- Draw a circle and cut it out. Then cut out a "slice" (a sector) of the circle as shown below.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-040.png]
- Curl the paper around so that $AB$ fits onto $AC$. You are now holding the curved face of a cone in your hand. Although this face is curved, it can be laid flat, so it is still a face.
- A cone has only one *edge*. The edge of a cone is not a straight line; it is a curve.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-041.png]
- The edge of a cone is the circumference of the circle that forms the base of the cone.
- A cone has only one *vertex*.
- The vertex of a cone is at the top of the cone.
- [Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-042.png]

The one vertex of a cone is also called the *apex* of the cone. From the base, the curved face becomes narrower until it forms a point at the top, which is the apex.

records.prompt_text:
Consider the diagram of the cone given below.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-043.png]

1. What is the name of the shaded area labelled $X$?
2. What shape is the shaded area labelled $X$?
3. Is the edge of a cone a straight line or a curve?
4. What is the name of the point labelled $Y$?
records.answer_text:
1. What is the name of the shaded area labelled $X$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

[Source image: https://electricbookworks.github.io/siyavula-open-textbooks-images/items/images/web/ebw-jss1-13-044.png]

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that narrows until it forms a point at the top, which is the apex.

Step 2: Identify the shaded area and give the correct answer.

The shaded area labelled $X$ is the base of the cone.

2. What shape is the shaded area labelled $X$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base.

Step 2: Identify the shape and give the correct answer.

The base of the cone, labelled $X$, is a circle.

3. Is the edge of a cone a straight line or a curve?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that tapers to a single point at the apex.

Step 2: Identify the edge of the cone and give the correct answer.

The edge of a cone is curved. The edge of a cone is the circumference of the circle that is the base of the cone.

4. What is the name of the point labelled $Y$?

Step 1: Recall the properties of a cone.

A cone has a circle as its base. It has only one curved side face that tapers to a single point at the apex.

Step 2: Identify the point labelled $Y$ and give the correct answer.

The point $Y$ is the vertex of the cone. It is also called the apex of the cone.

records.content_text:
A three-dimensional (3D) object has three dimensions that we can measure: length, breadth (or width), and height.

We use the main parts of a 3D object to describe its properties:
- A 3D object has faces. The faces can be flat or curved.
- The faces of a 3D object meet each other at an edge. The edge can be a straight line or a curve.
- The edges of a 3D object meet each other at a vertex. (Vertex is singular and vertices are plural.)
- The vertex at the top of a pyramid or a cone is called an apex.

**Properties of 3D objects**

- cube: 6 squares, 12 edges, 8 vertices
- cuboid: 3 pairs of equal rectangles = 6 rectangles, 12 edges, 8 vertices
- pyramid (square as base): 1 square + 4 triangles = 5 faces, 8 edges, 5 vertices
- cone: 1 circle + 1 curved face = 2 faces, 1 edge, 1 vertex
- cylinder: 2 circles + 1 curved face = 3 faces, 2 edges, 0 vertices
- sphere: 1 curved face, 0 edges, 0 vertices

Volume is the amount of space that an object takes up. It is measured in cubic units.

The volume of a prism is calculated using the formula $V_\text{prism} = \text{area of base} \times \text{height of the prism}$.

A cube is a prism. The formula for the volume of a cube is $V_\text{cube} = s \times s \times s\\$.

A cuboid is a prism. The formula for the volume of a cuboid is $V_\text{cuboid} = l \times b \times h$.
